facts.fact: Native programmatic display ad spending in the US is forecasted by eMarketer to reach $116.76 billion USD in 2025.
facts.quote: In 2025, native programmatic display ad spending in the US is forecasted to reach [$116.76 billion USD]

facts.fact: The first display ad was published by AT&T in 1994 on WIRED magazine's website and cost $30,000 USD.
facts.quote: The first one was published by AT&T back in 1994 on [WIRED magazine’s then-brand-new website]. It cost $30,000 USD

facts.fact: The first display ad by AT&T on WIRED's website reportedly had a 44% click-through rate.
facts.quote: It cost $30,000 USD and had a mind-boggling [44%](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/history-of-online-advertising) click-through rate (CTR).

facts.fact: Native advertising is typically purchased on a cost per thousand (CPM) basis, and the article states native's higher CTR can drive down cost per click.
facts.quote: Since ads are typically purchased on a cost per thousand (CPM) basis, the higher amount of clickthroughs can drive down your cost per click (CPC).

facts.fact: Native advertising conversions are usually, and recommended to be, measured only after the click.
facts.quote: conversions are usually (and are recommended to be) measured only after the click.

facts.fact: Native advertising can often be identified by labels such as "Sponsored," "Presented by," or "Recommended," which indicate that the content is paid for.
facts.quote: You can often identify native advertising by looking for labels such as “Sponsored,” “Presented by,” or “Recommended,” which indicate that the content is paid for.

facts.fact: According to the page, a native ad whose link leads to a different domain is likely designed to drive traffic elsewhere.
facts.quote: if it leads to a different domain, it’s likely a native ad designed to drive traffic elsewhere.
